text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a focused perf sweep across Mixtral-8x and Qwen-7b using the new chat-template v3. Seeing a reproducible latency bump when the system prompt + long convo history are present. Summary below.

maria: Profiling snippet (repro command at bottom):
```
model=mixtral-8x
seq_len=256->512 median per-token 12.3ms -> 18.9ms
kernel: preferred=flash_attn_v2, fallback=byte_kernel when tokenizer produces byte-fallback tokens
KV cache warmup: hits drop ~30% for inputs with special-system block
RoPE scale: 1.0 (baseline) vs 1.15 => p95 latency +22%
notes: kernel choose path toggles on q/k dim alignment and on "special_token_expansion"
```

aj: Can you paste the exact perf counters and the tokenizer diff? Is KV cache not being reused or are we hitting size-threshold evictions?

maria: Counters (excerpt):
```
perf.counters.kernel_select.flash_attn=68
perf.counters.kernel_select.byte_kernel=32
perf.counters.kv_cache.hits=0.71
perf.counters.kv_cache.evictions=0.04
perf.counters.batch_variance=0.28
profiling.tags=chat-template-v3,system-token-legacy
```
Also: observed that the system prompt contains some non-utf8 bytes after normalization which triggers our byte-fallback tokenizer path -> expands tokens from ~8 tokens to ~22 tokens for that block. That expansion increases seq_len, pushes to fallback kernel.

devon: Interesting — on Mixtral we have a kernel guard that checks (seq_len * dim_k) > THRESHOLD -> choose fused kernel. If the token count jumps due to byte-fallback, we exceed the threshold and hit the slower path. Also, RoPE scaling >1 changes matmul tiling and causes loss of fused qkv layout for some head counts (esp when heads not divisible by 8).

kevin: So two levers: 1) avoid tokenizer byte-fallback for system block (map to a single special token) 2) tweak kernel selection thresholds / batching heuristic. Which is lower risk?

maria: Short-term: change tokenizer mapping (force system -> single <SYS> token) and rerun. Medium-term: tune kernel selection to prefer fused kernel when variance is high, but need to be careful for memory.

perf-bot: :warning: regression-alert: perf delta detected on mixtral-8x chat-template-v3 p95 +19% (compare to baseline 1771003000). Auto-ticket created: #5621.

aj: Test matrix we should run:
- models: mixtral-8x, mixtral-3b, qwen-7b
- tokenizer: v2 (byte-fallback ON), v2-no-byte-fallback (map special tokens), v3-normalized
- RoPE scale: 1.0, 1.1, 1.15
- heads/kv remap: remap vs no-remap
- batching: dynamic (current) vs variance-aware (proposal)
Run microbench: 1000 requests each, cold/warm KV cache.

maria: I'll run the matrix on a small canary pool tonight (RUNTIME_DEBUG=1). Repro command: 
```bash
RUNTIME_DEBUG=1 ./bin/profile_infer --model mixtral-8x --tokenizer v2 --chat-template v3 --requests 1000 --ropescale 1.15
```
Pushing raw traces to perf-dashboard -> /dash/5621 (will link once uploaded).

devon: Proposal for batching heuristic tweak (pseudo):
```py
# prefer smaller batches if input token variance high
if token_variance(batch) > VAR_THRESH:
    effective_batch = max(1, int(batch_size * 0.6))
else:
    effective_batch = batch_size
# also lower kernel_select_threshold by 10% for mixtral family
```
This reduces tail latency by avoiding huge per-request seq_len spikes inside a big batch.

kevin: What about quantization path interaction? Byte-fallback + q4_0 has some slower dequantize hotspots. We should include quantization variants in the matrix.

maria: Good call — adding q8/q4 to the matrix. Also tagging eng-ml for tokenizer change (cc @devon @kevin). I'll update ticket #5621 with runs + recommended short-term mitigation: force single-token system mapping + canary of batching heuristic.

sre-bot: Noted. Scheduling canary: 4 gpus (dedicated-canary-3), window 02:00-04:00 UTC.

aj: Thanks — once canary data lands, we can decide rollback vs rollout of tokenizer mapping. :thumbsup:

maria: TL;DR: regression caused by tokenizer byte-fallback expanding system-block -> increases seq_len -> triggers slower kernel path and reduces KV cache hit rate. Short-term mitigation: tokenizer mapping; medium-term: kernel threshold/batch heuristics + RoPE/head alignment fixes.
